doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Adam Nussbaum: arts household, teaching himself drums, leaving City College
summary: Nussbaum came from an artistic family, taught himself drums, attended the Davis Center for five semesters, then learned on the New York scene.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I’d say pretty much the same thing. I didn’t really come from a musical household, I came from a very arts oriented household. My father was an artist and my mother was involved with acting and graphics. And I was the sole musician. And I had a lot of different experience when I was younger, I mean I studied the piano, I studied the bass, I studied the saxophone, but I just always wanted to play drums. So I kind of taught myself how to play drums after being inspired by an older cousin. And then I was always working in little rock bands, youth symphony, marching band, things like that, and got hip to jazz when I was about 14 or 15 and pretty much did it on my own. I did go to the Davis Center for Performing Arts which is a division of City College of New York for five semesters, because basically my parents said look while you go to school we’ll pay your rent. And we want you to go to school because of course we want you to be prepared. And I never finished school. Because I was in New York and I was having the opportunity to work with a lot of different people, doing a lot of little gigs for very little money, but for amazingly great wealth of experience. And I never finished school. And I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

just was out on the road. Being in New York City I had the opportunity to go to jam sessions, meet a lot of older musicians and have the opportunity to really have a hands on experience. So school was to fill in more of the theoretical aspects, you know, as far as learning about music, theory, harmony, stuff like that, which unfortunately I don’t know enough of. But being in New York City gave me the opportunity hands on to really learn about playing. So I’d say most of my education really comes from — the playing aspect — comes from being out there on the street more than through the academia.
